title: Record ESC-28: cancellation killed the current CI run and left the superseded one's verdict
body:
One row appended to `docs/escapes.md`. No code.

**What happened.** #191 sat blocked with three required checks red and nothing wrong with the branch. `gh run rerun` on one run turned everything green without touching a line.

**The mechanism, measured.** Two commits were pushed to that branch: `affb64d`, then `32bd547` (the auto-updater merging the base in). Each produced a `pull_request` CI run, and **both share one concurrency group** — `ci.yml` keys on `ci-<workflow>-<ref>`, and `github.ref` is `refs/pull/191/merge` for every `pull_request` event on that pull request.

The cancellation then went the wrong way:

```
newer run (32bd547 — the commit that would merge)
  checks / template-sync / acceptance-criteria   CANCELLED 12:14:28

older run (affb64d — superseded)
  plan                started 12:14:40   FAILED 12:14:46
```

The superseded run outlived the current one by eighteen seconds and its failure became the reported status. `ci.yml`'s own comment states the intent — *"a SUPERSEDED run is pure waste — it is testing a commit nobody will merge"* — and the outcome was the exact inverse.

**Why it reads as unfixable rather than as a cause.** The check list showed `checks` twice, once passing and once failing. Nothing compares a reported check against the commit it ran on, so a stale verdict looks like a fresh one. And nothing retries a cancelled required check, so *cancelled*, *still running* and *never started* all present identically: a pull request that will not merge, with nothing to point at.

**ESC-20** already records that every gate judges one pull request in isolation and none sees the queue. This is the same blindness one level down — none of them sees the run history of the pull request it is judging.

**The fix worth building** is the first candidate: key the concurrency group on the **commit**, not the pull request. Two runs on two different commits then never contend, and cancellation only ever removes a genuine duplicate of the same tree. The row also names a cheaper mitigation and one broader catch — treating a cancelled required check as a failure that retries once, rather than as a silence.

**Not in scope, and my error, not a gate's.** What put a second commit on that branch at all was #191 failing `escape-refs.sh` for citing ESC-27 before ESC-27 had landed. That is the ordering rule **ESC-18** and **ESC-20** already record, and it needs no new row — I ran `plan-resolve.sh` and `plan-lint.sh` on that branch and not `escape-refs.sh`.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh`, `escapes-append-only.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
